top_stories.title: India's Gen-Z Cockroach Janta Party channels youth anger but faces offline hurdles - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: The popularity of **Abhijeet Dipke**'s online satirical group, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has grown rapidly in India, fueled by concerns over youth unemployment and dissatisfaction with the government.  Dipke's movement, which gained traction after a comment by India's Chief Justice comparing unemployed youth to cockroaches, has attracted millions of followers, surpassing the 9.3 million followers of **Narendra Modi**'s Bharatiya Janata Party. Despite its rapid growth, CJP faces challenges in organizing and mobilizing for protests due to concerns over government crackdowns on dissent.  Analysts warn that while CJP represents a significant shift in public sentiment, it remains unclear if the group can translate online frustration into tangible political action.

top_stories.title: UN ‘adds Israel to blacklist’ for conflict-related sexual violence | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **United Nations** has added **Israel** to its blacklist of parties suspected of or responsible for sexual violence in conflict zones.  **Israeli** ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, announced that Israel will sever ties with the UN secretary-general, **Antonio Guterres**, over the upcoming report. The decision was met with anger from the **Israeli** government and foreign ministry, who accused the **UN** of being politicized and corrupt.  The **UN** has cited credible information regarding sexual violence committed by Israeli security forces against Palestinian detainees in prisons and detention centers, prompting a response from **Israel** that it will sue the New York Times for reporting on alleged rape by its forces.

top_stories.title: Villas, cars and cash: Italy seizes dead Mafia mobster's millions
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Anti-mafia investigators** in Italy have seized assets worth over €200 million linked to the late Sicilian mafia boss Matteo Messina Denaro. The funds, which include cash, companies, and real estate holdings, are believed to be proceeds from decades of drug trafficking.  The operation targeted the network of Messina Denaro, who died in custody after his arrest in 2023, and involved multiple countries including Spain, Switzerland, and the Cayman Islands. **Giovanni Melillo**, head of the National Anti-Mafia Prosecutor's Office, called the operation "strategically significant" for disrupting the Cosa Nostra's criminal activities and preventing its reformation.

top_stories.title: EU fines Temu for failing to stop sale of illegal and dangerous products | European Commission | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The European Commission** has fined **Temu**, a Chinese shopping website, €200 million for failing to prevent the sale of illegal and dangerous products. The fine is the second-highest ever imposed under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) and follows a 19-month investigation that found unsafe products on the platform, including baby toys, electronics, and clothing. **Temu** has the right to appeal the decision and claims it disagrees with the fine's proportionality. The company says it is taking steps to strengthen risk assessment and user protection.

top_stories.title: US Treasury threatens Oman with sanctions over Hormuz Strait | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent** warned **Oman** that the US will impose sanctions if it facilitates tolls in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions between the two countries.  Bessent stated that Washington "will not tolerate" any fees imposed on commercial ships in the strategic waterway and emphasized that all nations should reject Iran's efforts to disrupt commerce. This follows President Donald Trump's threats against **Oman**, a key US ally known for its neutrality, over potential Iranian-Omani control of the Strait.  The US has been indirectly negotiating with Iran to reach an agreement for a comprehensive end to the war, and control over the Hormuz Strait has emerged as a major point of disagreement.

top_stories.title: Govt. plans security protocol for fishing harbours under CISF oversight - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)** will oversee the security of around 1,200 fishing harbours and landing sites across India as part of a plan to strengthen the country's coastline. The **Union Home Ministry** aims to implement this framework after assigning CISF personnel to secure 250 seaports. This move follows guidelines issued by the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** in 2023, and is intended to provide a uniform security template for all coastal areas.  The government's objective is to ensure the safety of fisherfolk and prevent potential threats like those seen during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

top_stories.title: Trump's face could appear on US $250 bill - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump's** likeness is being considered for a new $250 bill, a proposal that would be the first time a living person appears on US currency in over 150 years.  The **Treasury Department**, under the Trump administration, has pushed forward with the plan despite concerns about federal law prohibiting depictions of living presidents on money. The printing bureau director, Patricia Solimene, was reassigned after raising objections to the proposal. This move has sparked criticism from Democrats and accusations of a cult of personality around the 79-year-old leader.

top_stories.title: Israel hits Lebanese capital Beirut in 'targeted strike'
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Israel** carried out a targeted strike on the Lebanese capital, Beirut, for the second time since a ceasefire last month. The **IDF** stated that the attack was in response to Hezbollah attacks and aimed at Ali al-Husni, head of an Iranian militia.  The strikes came after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced an expansion of a ground operation following Hezbollah drone attacks on troops and civilians. At least 11 people were killed in two sets of Israeli strikes which hit Tyre and an area to the city's east early on Thursday. The escalation threatens to derail peace talks between the US, Israel, and Iran, while Lebanon faces displacement and humanitarian concerns.

top_stories.title: Image of Thai police in sparkly dresses with handcuffed suspect turns out to be AI fake | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Thai** police officers posted an image of themselves in elaborate festival-style dresses arresting a drug dealer on their Facebook page.  However, the image was later revealed to be an AI-generated fake, prompting media outlets to retract their stories and highlighting the challenges of verifying images online. The incident underscores the need for improved verification methods as AI-generated imagery becomes increasingly prevalent.

top_stories.title: US, Mexico, Canada announce Ebola-related travel measures for World Cup | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **US**, **Mexico**, and **Canada** have announced aligned public health travel measures for individuals coming from African regions at risk of Ebola as the World Cup begins next month. The **WHO** declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo a public health emergency of international concern, prompting governments to implement containment measures.  The measures include bans on entry for certain citizens and residents, as well as quarantine requirements for those who have been in affected areas recently.
